meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. On what basis did you enter it?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.

Different editions differ, and a student can misattribute a critic's line without a machine writing it for him. Show me the page in Owen's essay where he quotes it, and tell me which act and scene he says it comes from.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

Be very careful with your next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and you just brought my daughter into my son's meeting. I'm writing that down, and it's going to the principal with everything else.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology, and that nothing about this appear on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Back at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the matter taken to the principal, which is not the fair outcome, since the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting never got close to it.
What moved her: Pointing to a quotation in the essay that does not appear in Hamlet, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own work, and something she could check herself, so she stopped attacking and asked to see the page.
What cost ground: Bringing up her daughter's old case and suggesting it runs in the family, because it attacked her family instead of the essay and sent her straight back to the principal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never came near that night, since no times or dates of writing were raised; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the page and the act and scene, turn the essay toward her and let her search the play for that line herself, and leave her daughter out of it entirely.
